body:
### Summary

I am trying to have a more generic environment + script management than `hatch`, `nox`,` tox`, etc. PEP723 scripts come close to this, but they don't have clear support for project extras or dependency groups.

The project extras can potentially be solved with using the `project[extra]` syntax and/or the path navigation. The issue would be, how to convey that this dependency should be installed as editable?

Dependency groups are more unclear since there is no format for defining these as dependencies.

There is the [`tool.uv.tasks`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/5903) proposal, but this just shifts the definition from `hatch` to `uv` and still end up locked to an environment. My preference here is to use the standards defined for it PEP723 being the case here, and somehow extend the definition or settings to tell the runner `uv`/`hatch` etc. how to prepare an environment and reuse the definitions given in `pyproject.toml`. For example

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# /// script
# [tool.environment]
# name = "docs"
# root = ".."
# dependency-groups = ["docs"]
# ///
```
